title: Geometric descent and ordered multiplication of vector integration traces
statement:
Let $N\geq1$, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring killed by $N$, and let $B$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. For a vector bundle $\pi:E\to B$ of constant rank $r\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], work in the ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Set $W_\pi=A_E(r)[2r]$ using ordinary Tate lines [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], and use the actual integration $t_\pi:R\pi_!W_\pi\to A_B[0]$ of [def-amb-vector-integration]. All compact-support exchanges and compositors below are the proper/open normalized maps of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons].

For every $g:B'\to B$ with Noetherian $B'$, form the pullback bundle $\pi':E'=E\times_BB'\to B'$ and its projection $g':E'\to E$. Let $C_W:g^*R\pi_!W_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_!g'^*W_\pi$ be exchange and $l:g'^*W_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}W_{\pi'}$ the ordinary Tate pullback comparison. Then
$$t_{\pi'}\circ R\pi'_!(l)\circ C_W=g^*(t_\pi).$$

For locally free modules $F,G$ on $B$ of ranks $r,s\geq0$, let $p:E(G)\to B$, $q:E(F\oplus G)\to E(G)$ and $h=pq$. The symmetric-algebra total space $E(F\oplus G)$ is canonically $E(F)\times_BE(G)$, with $q$ the pulled-back rank-$r$ bundle. Identify $W_h\cong q^*W_p\otimes_A^LW_q$ by the ordered Tate/shift associator. With $\alpha:Rp_!Rq_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rh_!$ and the canonical compact-support projection map $P_q$ (proper projection map and open-extension tensor comparison on a compactification [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection, lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor]), the actual traces satisfy
$$t_h\circ\alpha_{W_h}=t_p\circ Rp_!\bigl((1_{W_p}\otimes t_q)\circ P_{q;W_p,W_q}^{-1}\bigr).$$
These equations hold for every compactification triangle used to define $\alpha$, and are unchanged by exchanging the two ordered blocks with the canonical coordinate permutation. Each trace source has cohomology only in degree zero and its trace is an isomorphism. Rank zero gives the identity adjunction trace under $E(0)=B$; the empty base gives the unique maps. No affinity of intersections of trivializing opens is assumed.

proof.text: Reuse vectorIntegration_cohomology_zero for concentration. Choose a locally free frame cover and normalized affine trace data. The defining normalization of the actual glued integration identifies its restriction on each frame with exchange, coefficient isomorphisms, and the affine trace counit. Each factor is invertible, so every restriction of the actual integration is invertible. Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff, exact inverse-image compatibility with cohomology, and jointly surjective sheaf inverse-image conservativity to deduce global invertibility. No inverse sheaf maps need to be glued again.

source.place: paragraph 2: specified affine-space counits, simultaneous trivializations, degree-zero sheaf descent

proof.text: The equality-on-a-cover helper is proved directly for a source isomorphic to a single degree-zero sheaf. Fullness of singleFunctor expresses both derived maps as sheaf maps, and etaleDegreeZeroHomEquiv_map identifies their inverse-image restrictions with those of the sheaf maps. Jointly faithful inverse images (from jointly surjective isomorphism conservativity) identify these sheaf maps. For uniqueness of normalized integration, similarly express any normalized arrow using the fixed heart identification, then apply the defining existence-and-uniqueness of vectorIntegrationGluing to its sheaf component. Frame independence itself is already part of the existing glued integration and is not reproved.

proof.text: Form b from the actual base-change exchange and the coefficient comparison. Choose independent frame covers V_i of F on S and U_j of f*F on T. Their intersections f inverse(V_i) intersect U_j cover T, as proved pointwise. On each such open W, use its inclusions into U_j and f inverse(V_i), followed by the restricted f, to supply the two factorizations into S. Choose normalized affine trace data, identify its Tate transport with the supplied transport by ordinaryFiniteTwistTransport_unique, and apply the local two-frame base-change calculation with the defining normalization equations of the existing glued integrations. For global equality, b followed by the fixed degree-zero identification of C_f*F identifies the common source with a single sheaf. Express each of the two arrows as an image under singleFunctor, transport their equal restrictions to localized sheaf morphisms by etaleDegreeZeroHomEquiv_map, and use jointly faithful sheaf inverse images (deduced from their isomorphism conservativity) to identify the two sheaf maps. Reassociate b.hom to recover exactly the stated equation. No affinity of intersections or extra condition on f is used.

proof.text: Choose independent frame covers V_i of F and U_j of G and define O_(i,j)=V_i∩U_j. Prove pointwise that these opens cover S. Form the isomorphism from Rp_!Rq_!W_h to the single degree-zero sheaf of F⊕G: compose the actual compact-support compositor, Rh_! of the inverse coefficient transport, the inverse product exchange, the inverse-image identity comparison, and the defining normalized heart identification vectorIntegrationGluing. Apply the already proved derived_eq_of_cover helper with this isomorphism and the simultaneous frame cover. The remaining goal on each O_(i,j) is exactly the local ordered multiplication calculation, unfolded only at the product-presentation constructions. This is a genuine local-to-global reduction, with no assumption that intersections are affine. The coefficient transport, exchange and decomposition parameters of the local lemma are supplied by the original definitions; their canonical-map constraints are discharged separately by unfolding each definition and reflexivity. Prove the defining equation for vectorTraceSumIntegration separately and transport it by congrArg through restriction and the compositor, then compose with the local equality; no broad normalization of the outer functors is used.

Expand only the four outer factors of compactSupportProjectionMap; the two signed symmetries and the exact-derived pullback comparison are isomorphisms, and direct image preserves them.

proof.text: For the every-compactification-triangle equality, rewrite unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso by its tower equation. Expanding purityCompactComposition and the whiskering components gives the identical composite by associativity. This clause needs no direct-sum integration equation and is independent of the compactification choices.

proof.text: For block swap, form b from the actual swap exchange and coefficient comparison. Transport the existing G-plus-F trace back through b. Restrict biproduct braiding to any supplied frame of F-plus-G and transport the rank equality to produce a G-plus-F frame. Its defining normalization equation and the local swap theorem normalize the transported map; the proved uniqueness helper identifies it with the original F-plus-G trace. Cancel b with its inverse. For rank zero, form b from the actual zero-square exchange and transport the displayed identity trace back through b. The local rank-zero theorem normalizes this map, uniqueness identifies it with the actual integration, and cancellation gives the equation. On an empty base, apply derived inverse-image conservativity to the empty family and the map from the coefficient unit to zero. This proves that the target is a zero object, so all arrows into it agree.

tool_uses.why: Generic heart-valued morphism gluing is used to check trace equalities on frame covers; no smooth purity theorem is used.
Ordinary etale Tate pullback/tensor composition supplies source comparisons for arbitrary finite A.
Generic compatibility of the actual projection with base change identifies the direct-sum formula on opens.
Ordinary etale proper projection gives invertibility and the signed tensor normalization of P.
Generic ordinary etale open tensor comparison supplies the open factor of P.
Generic symmetric-algebra universal property identifies the direct sum algebra as a coproduct by checking generators.
Generic relative-Spec anti-equivalence turns the symmetric-algebra coproduct into the stated total-space product.

Generic relative-Spec base change identifies the fibre product E x_B B' (and E(F) x_B E(G) -> E(G)) with the vector bundle of the pulled-back module, so its integration and pulled-back frames are defined.
